cands.bio: Republican candidate for New Jersey's 9th District. Clifton City Council member since 2019 and Clifton Board of Education member from 2013 or 2014 to 2019. Rutgers finance graduate. Her campaign site says she worked as a Treasury bank examiner. Ballotpedia lists earlier work in Passaic County finance and career development.
cands.gaps: We could not find her votes or sponsored measures on the Clifton City Council or Board of Education, so there is little on what she did in office. We found no stated position on data centers, development or land protection, property-tax elimination, limits on investor or foreign land buying, or gun policy. Her site does not specify a teacher pay raise. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for her. Her biography has gaps and conflicts: the sources disagree on her birthplace, the year she joined the school board, and her early career. No independent confirmation of her Treasury job was found. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey.

qual.background: She has held local elected office, on the Clifton Board of Education (elected 2013, two terms) and the Clifton City Council (since 2019). She has a Rutgers finance degree. Her campaign site says she was a U.S. Treasury bank examiner. Ballotpedia says she worked in Passaic County Community College's finance department and at Passaic County One Stop.
qual.why: Local elected office and a finance background put her in the middle band. She has no legislative or executive experience at the state or federal level, and her council and board records were not available.
qual.label: Local elected office and a finance background put her in the middle band. She has no legislative or executive experience at the state or federal level, and her council and board records were not available.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says she supports school choice, including charter schools and education savings accounts, with funding that follows the student. Her site mentions no teacher raise.

pro-life.evidence: Says she is 'proudly pro-life' and that abortion should be 'rare and limited,' with exceptions for rape, incest or the mother's life. This is narrower than a no-exceptions position.

workers-first.evidence: Says she supports President Trump's border security policies and wants Border Patrol and ICE equipped to arrest and deport violent criminals. She also supports legal immigration. Her site does not address H-1B.

back-police-order.evidence: Says she supports fully funding law enforcement and strongly opposes efforts to defund or weaken police.

cands.bio: Democrat who has represented New Jersey's 9th District in the U.S. House since January 2025. She served in the NJ Assembly (1997–2012) and State Senate (2012–2025), and chaired the Assembly Appropriations Committee. Earlier she worked for the City of Paterson, including as business administrator.

controversies.text: Federal records show $5,000 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; 1 trip paid for by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's affiliate.
Missed 0 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (0.0%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include EMILY's List, New Jersey Citizen Action and Humane World Action Fund.
The New Jersey AFL-CIO endorsed her in 2013 (and the state AFL-CIO in 2011) for State Senate.

cands.gaps: We could not find Pou's stated positions or actions on data centers, limits on out-of-state or institutional home buyers, H-1B visas, gun laws, abortion, or school vouchers and charters. We found no documented statements on development or data centers, and no pledges about donor or PAC money. Her state legislative votes and sponsored bills were not available in the pages reviewed. The original reporting on the Israel trip was not available, so her response and the details of that criticism are missing. Her exact year of moving to New Jersey is not needed because she says she was born and raised in Paterson, but the birthplace comes from her campaign site rather than an independent record.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).

qual.background: About 27 years in the New Jersey Legislature (Assembly 1997–2012, Senate 2012–2025), including six years chairing the Assembly Appropriations Committee and chairing the Senate Commerce Committee. Before that she held city administration roles in Paterson, including director of human services and business administrator. She has served in the U.S. House since 2025.
qual.why: Long legislative service, budget and appropriations leadership, and executive experience in city government all fit the lawmaking, oversight and budgeting work of a House member.
qual.label: Long legislative service, budget and appropriations leadership, and executive experience in city government all fit the lawmaking, oversight and budgeting work of a House member.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign website says she is fighting to increase funding for police departments and programs that bolster community safety, and that she will always support funding for police and firefighters.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Her 2013 campaign website said she was committed to providing property tax relief and co-chaired one of four 2006 special-session committees on property taxes, sixteen of whose recommendations were enacted. This is the campaign's own account.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her 2013 campaign website said she sponsored 2004 legislation to dedicate park and open space development funding to densely populated communities. This is the campaign's own account.

workers-first.evidence: Voted Nay on the Laken Riley Act (S.5), which requires DHS to detain certain undocumented immigrants arrested for theft-related offenses; the bill passed 263-156 (per Ballotpedia's key-votes list).
